label: late original-phase u/q/2/t/p/z input in sequences starting with i/x/m/d/l/r
explanation: Fires only in the original (input) phase at t >= 3, never at the delimiter or during copying. It is mostly active at later input positions: the rate rises with orig_idx (0.8% at t=3 up to 9% at t=8) and is highest on the last input before <DEL>. It is driven by the current input token: u is strongest, then q, 2 and t, then p, z, j, g and e. Digits 1 and 3 and most other letters rarely trigger it. It is strongly modulated by the first token of the sequence: i, x, m, d, l and r give a 3-5x lift, so this looks like a conjunction of the current token with leftover state from the start of the sequence. Activations are mostly on the first occurrence of the token (in_first carries 88% of the mass). The top examples are u/q/z on the last input step of sequences starting with i/d/x. Given the token set, t >= 3 and phase 0, there are still many false positives, so the gating by earlier context is only partly captured (dev F1 about 0.51, mass recall 0.59). No clean summary of the earlier context improved on first_tok.
